title: Onboarding-to-Retirement routing playbook for version-locked models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational playbook and runtime implementation for safe transitions from model onboarding through long-term version pinning to final retirement. This task defines the automated routing rules, staged retirement waves, and compatibility checks that allow us to: (1) publish performance profiles at onboarding time, (2) honor customer version locks, and (3) perform graceful fallbacks and retirements across regions and variant families without violating latency SLOs or causing correctness regressions. The design emphasizes a lightweight controller ("fallback-sentinel") that monitors per-region health and a compatibility matrix that rates viable fallback candidates (same-architecture quantized variants, cross-region replicas, or last-known-good hosted variant).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Fallback-sentinel prototype deployed to canary: reacts to simulated region GPU outage and fails over to a region-compatible variant within configured 30s window.
2) Version-locked routes respect customer pin; when pinned variant is unavailable, the system follows the configured escalation policy (regional-variant -> cross-region -> notify + hold) and records all decisions to audit logs.
3) Publishing onboarding performance profile hooks into model-catalog so runtime can choose kernel/quantization policy automatically.
4) Retirement wave script can demote traffic in 3 staged waves with metrics gates (error rate, p95 latency, qualitative eval) and supports automatic rollback.
5) End-to-end integration tests added to runtime CI exercising at least 3 fallback paths, with synthetic traffic and acceptance thresholds for latency and token-cost regressions.
updates: 2025-02-12 - Initial design spike completed: defined 'fallback-sentinel' as a controller that evaluates region health, variant compatibility score, and policy TTL. Spike notes in Confluence.

2025-02-15 - Architecture review with Runtime/Platform: agreed on compatibility scoring that weights architecture match (same model family > quantization parity), KV-cache warmup cost, and cross-region latency. Action: Marco to add scoring library to runtime-core.

2025-02-18 - PM feedback (D. Huang): prefer conservative default policy for pinned customers: 'hold-and-alert' rather than auto-downgrade for first outage event. Added policy knobs for customer tiers.
2025-02-20 - Implemented sentinel alerting hooks and audit-log events schema. Created PR for audit schema: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2387. QA to craft synthetic outage test.

2025-02-24 - Incident simulation (INC-2025-67 north-east GPU outage) replayed in staging: sentinel detected degradation, attempted regional-variant fallback but cache-warmup penalty exceeded threshold -> executed cross-region failover per policy. Observed p95 spike of +120ms for 2 minutes, then returned to baseline. Lessons: need pre-warm path for KV cache on compatible fallbacks.

2025-02-27 - Design update: added 'warm-warm' pre-warm step during onboarding (retain small per-variant KV snapshot for top-k fallbacks) and a weight-decay retirement wave to avoid sudden traffic shifts.
